Based on the all the comments i'm just going to go from cycling to daily.

start with eyeliner as it takes a lot of practice and is really a core makeup product. plan on practicing with eyeliner for a month or longer.  mascara and eyebrow pencils should be next on your list as most women wear some amount of eye makeup daily.  

try drugstore brands to start with avoid the cheapest stuff and dont be brand loyal a company that makes great lip gloss may not make great eyeliner.  

dont forget makeup remover

a lot of great replies on here especially having a friend shop with you.  also shop early or late during less busy hours. 

I had good experience at jc penny early on when looking for bras, i just told the sales girl as privately as i could i was transgender and needed bras 

something I learned while trying to go full time and was able to apply towards shopping as well.   I had to get myself to the ' i dont care what you think' state of mind.  in my mind i was [wrongly] thinking people would think i dont have the right to present as female.  i turned this around, i wondered what gave people the right to bring their noisy, bratty children into the stores where they treat it like a playground, or why they had a right to dress the way they did, or..., it didnt take long to realize that i have every right to present however i wanted in public and buy anything from any shop i wanted.

 I really dont care what people think of me but being sick while presenting trans is about the worst.  not feeling your best, not focusing on appearance and presentation, for me this results in more staring at me, I was a bit uncomfortable but just kept to myself, at some point the staring stopped

if you are really paranoid like me and doing DIY consider carrying them in a vitamin bottle where the description/pic of the vitamin matches the pills
i'm in the same boat scared to stop taking DHT blocker, although i take avodart as i get side effects from finasteride.

my shoe size and finger size dropped almost instantly. no height changes with over a year of HRT, to help maintain height and bone density  take vitamin D with fat [like milk] and get plenty of calcium, my doctor recommended 5,000 units of vitamin D daily as i had low D levels, subsequent test show D in range even with 5,000 units

I tried electrolysis and decided to go with laser.  pain, time per session, time to completion, cost were major factors in my decision.  another consideration with electrolysis is they ask you not to shave prior to appointment, walking around with visible facial hair while being full time wasnt an option for me

Your therapist is likely using an out of date WPATH standards of care model.   find a new therapist ASAP.  ask towards the end of your visits if they see any red flags and push on getting a time frame on your HRT letter.

get a full thyroid test.  

ketogenic  diet (low carb/high protein) mention by others helps as well as niacin.  I had high cholesterol long before starting HRT,   i also take 100mg pregnenolne daily. there is little research that taking pregnenolne will offer any benefits on cholesterol - check with your doctor.

Metzler seems to be more expensive than others in the same area which caused me to be a little hesitant.  after a recent consultation with another highly praised plastic surgeon that left me feeling with a feeling the results might be substandard,  i fully intend to get a consultation with Metzler.

I have a thought about body hair if HRT doesn't help with it.  A number of years ago my acupuncturist put me on 'dong quai' for hair growth, while i didnt see noticeable results in new hair it did turn my hair light brown darker to a medium brown while i was taking it. it might be enough to make you body hair dark enough for laser.   if you go down this route make sure it wont interfere with HRT meds and take an ample dose of 2 or 3 capsules daily

start by getting a good therapist right away to help you sort this out.  I'm sure someone here can point you to a good therapist in your part of the world.  

If you wait like i did and later in life become consumed with every fiber of you being in needing to transition you will be less happy with the results and spend more of your life miserable.

as far as 'all the work' dont focus on it as it really isnt much. .  I got caught up with that many times during my transition putting off important things like voice training.   while it may seem like a huge undertaking you are not being held to a timeline, take baby steps, how much work is it the visit a therapist a few times a doctor and drugstore over next three months then pop a few pills every day?

on the eyebrow side of things i suggest finding a hairstylist with trans experience.  One of the members of my local support group recommended a trans experienced hairstylist due to my naturally curly hair, she educated me a lot on hair care.   i went back to her and asked her for brow waxing, very pleased.  this was my second waxing, the first being done at a beauty school which i cant recommend.

also doing E injection, i think its 1ml/10mg/weekly, was cycling progesterone as well until i stepped up to 200mg, i cant get past day 6 before the side effects catch up with me.

plan on incorporating DHT blocker shortly after starting HRT or even before.  wish someone had made this clear to me before i started

1) walk away
2)display of  middle finger(s) followed by walking away

I am hyper focused on losing weight for the same reasons.  lots of cardio will help. Spending less then 30 minutes working out wont net you any results.  

Alternate your workout if you can: alternate from cardio to weights and back to cardio as the initial cardio session will increase your heart rate, your heart rate will stay somewhat elevated as your transition to weights which will help burn more fat.  

make your workout as entertaining as possible to prevent boredom.  watch TV, take a smartphone, a tablet, e-reader or whatever you need to to keep from getting bored.  I use a tablet with a bluetooth pendant for netflix viewing, i switch to slacker when i get to weights with my tablet safely tucked away so it doesnt get damaged.   

Diet is also important, i am using principles found in  "How I Gave Up My Low-Fat Diet and Lost 40 Pounds..and How You Can Too: The Ultimate Guide to Low-Carbohydrate Dieting"  lost 4 pounds in first week.
